closureMethod: Trace every family across core, wire schema, CLI, host/hook, persistence, list/export, consumer and named focused positive/negative checks. This matrix and retained schema bounds constitute the semantic dispositions; the source census is discovery/review material, not an assertion that regex results alone prove closure. Physical host failure thresholds beyond concrete runtime/format capacities remain unknown.

families.focusedPositive: 120 same-kind hits; >24 query terms; parent chain24; large expansions and full replay

families.removedProductCeilings: scalar4096/table8192; category/name/model/effort/note; variable name64/value1024; escalation100; concurrent32; tau100; injection16KiB; excerpt4096
families.currentBehavior: complete strings/tables; positive safe numbers accepted; quota percentage semantics retained; project isolation applies to all declared controls

families.currentBehavior: ustar header name100 bytes and fixed 512-byte blocks remain; native port maximum65535; SHA truncation defines stable ids rather than truncating user data

families.family: Verification / approved run windows / diagnostic summaries
families.removedProductCeilings: none of these are re-labelled as immutable product capacities
families.currentBehavior: fixed governed test child-group slots8, time/capture run windows, 60s incremental wakeup, diagnostic samples120/200/256/512 remain as verification/session budgets; they can stop that verification run and do not authorize shortening product data or claiming host capacity
families.retainedBasis: approved verification execution method/budget boundary; changing those run budgets or weakening refusal gates requires its own authority; current Pack does not raise approved gate budgets
families.focusedPositive: focused source checks remain separate from official task gates; run receipts retain complete stdout/stderr
families.focusedNegative: official worktree build/typecheck repository admission refusal preserved; output overflow yields explicit incomplete/refusal, never green
